english.title: Master of a coasting ship where goods taken on board / removed at sea / outside UK
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the master of a coasting ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..),

(A)_[upon which goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..) were taken on board]_
(B)_[from which goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..) were removed]_

at sea or at a place outside the United Kingdom
english.legislation: Contrary to section 74(1)(a) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
is the master of a coasting ship
upon which goods are taken on board / removed
at sea / at a place outside the United Kingdom

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 74(2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979 provides that any goods which are shipped and carried coastwise, or which, having been carried coastwise, are unloaded in any place in the United Kingdom, otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of sections 69 to 71 or regulations made under section 73 of the Act or which are brought to any place for the purpose of being so shipped and carried coastwise, shall be liable to forfeiture.
